items.summary: More than 120 member states concluded a week-long conference in Geneva under the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons, but an agreement to discuss regulating autonomous weapons over the next two years fell short of what rights groups consider urgent. The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) warned that rapid development and fielding of AI-driven systems may make regulation too late; ICRC director Dr Cordula Droege said artificial intelligence is being deployed in battlefields and possibly already in weapon systems, making it harder to reverse once unregulated use spreads. Autonomous weapons are defined as military systems acting without human supervision through AI or robotics, with examples cited including Israeli AI-assisted target banks in Gaza, semi-autonomous drones with last-mile capability in the Ukraine-Russia war, and a July incident where an AI-guided Russian drone killed three civilians near Zaporizhzhia after missing its intended petrol station. The ICRC president Mirjana Spoljaric Egger and UN secretary general António Guterres called for a legally binding instrument with clear prohibitions; the ICRC specifically urged banning autonomous weapons against personnel, ensuring predictable behavior, and restricting use to military objectives. Rights groups warned that delays risk letting private industry and militaries set usage norms, citing civilian harm in Gaza from AI-assisted targeting of civilians and loosely linked militants, an Iranian strike on an elementary school killing 156 people reportedly due to faulty AI intelligence, and proliferation as non-state actors such as Yemen's Houthis used Claude to program ballistic missiles. Future of Life Institute head Anna Hehir warned that further delay could produce mass civilian harm from emerging swarm capabilities involving hundreds or thousands of autonomous drones acting simultaneously. A senior diplomat characterized the conference outcome as a failure to demonstrate political will, noting substantive regulation had been absent for 13 years.
items.title: UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons Conference Falls Short of Agreement on Autonomous Weapon Regulation

items.summary:
An e-bike journalist who has covered the industry for nearly two decades presents a list of accessories he personally relies on, framed as items he actually uses rather than an exhaustive or definitively best-in-class ranking. The central theme is that most days require only an e-bike and a helmet; the listed gear represents products battle-tested over years of professional testing, recreational riding, exercise, and daily transportation for his car-free family.

For bike security, he recommends two locks used nearly every day: Seatylock's FoldyLock Forever folding lock, which he states is certified as the world's strongest folding lock with an ART 3-star rating from the Stichting ART Foundation (certified three years ago), and a Mason 220 U-lock. He also uses a smaller, cheaper, brightly colored FoldyLock Compact for easier carrying. Regarding AirTags, he hides multiple units—stating that one is 'for amateurs'—using a four-pack costing $79, which he notes is around half the cost of a solid e-bike lock, plus an AliExpress bell with a hidden compartment ($4) and other holders (a $5 water bottle holder and an $8 rear reflector).

On safety gear, he gravitates toward UNIT 1 helmets for integrated lighting and MIPS on models like the FARO, and the lighter NEON helmet rated for faster 28 mph riding. He wears a Beyond Riders protective hoodie with CE Level 2 armor at elbows, shoulders, chest, and spine, while noting no hoodie makes a crash harmless.

For convenience and maintenance, he lists H2O Audio TRI ULTRA PRO bone-conduction headphones (tested on rides as long as 3 hours), Knog Oi Prima bell (~$32), Tannus tire liners for flat protection including runflat capability, a Topeak Ratchet Stick ($48) that he has used for around 6 years at roughly $8 per year of cost, and an AliExpress waterproof-style pannier bought for around $25.

Among the cheapest items are plastic handlebar jacks purchased on AliExpress for barely more than $1. He also recommends a ZOOM suspension dropper seatpost installed on his Ride1Up Roadster V3; he reports it took nearly two hours to install because that model lacked internal cable routing, requiring him to drill a small hole in the seat tube—an action he explicitly does not recommend and warns can compromise frame integrity or void warranties.

Finally, for photography while riding, he uses the HOVERAir X1 Pro Max drone, which folds small enough to forget it is there; he notes its obstacle avoidance is poor when flying sideways or backward. He closes by reiterating that most of this gear is not necessary and that casual riders may find some expensive items unnecessary.

The text contains no stated limitations beyond the author's own caveats: no lock makes a bike theft-proof, AirTags are not dedicated anti-theft GPS trackers and include Apple anti-stalking features, tire liners do not prevent every flat, protective gear does not make crashes harmless, obstacle avoidance is weak in certain flight directions, and drilling into frames should be avoided.
items.title: A Professional E-Bike Journalist Recommends His Daily-Used Accessories

items.summary: A player testing Grand Theft Auto 6, which launched Thursday and reportedly generated $3.79 billion in first-day sales per Take-Two, reports that electric vehicles are depicted as ordinary traffic in the game's version of Miami (Vice City), a notable shift from the series' long-standing treatment of EVs as punchlines beginning with Coil models introduced around 2013 and expanded via GTA Online updates starting late 2017. The player notes EV adoption increases geographically within the game—concentrated in Vice City while remaining rare in the Keys, mirroring real-world patterns where Florida posted a 9.4% share of new passenger vehicle sales in Q2 2026 versus 7.4% nationally per Southern Alliance for Clean Energy—and includes EV-specific elements such as Tesla and Porsche lookalikes (the Coil Raiden and Pfister Neon), public fast chargers branded 'ReVolt America' after Electrify America, a large charging hub at a power plant, gas cars blocking charger stalls, battery levels requiring plugs instead of fuel pumps, and the first mainline game where energy consumption is tracked. Kotaku's range test cited in the article found a Tesla Model 3 lookalike lasted 20 minutes and 23 seconds on charge versus 18 minutes and 31 seconds for a Banshee sports car over the same highway loop; Wccftech counted 120 EV chargers against 57 gas stations. Electrify America responded to the parody with a statement declining in-game participation while wishing ReVolt well, though all game ReVolt stations reportedly functioned correctly during testing. The player identifies home charging as an unimplemented feature—unavailable because early-game properties are rented—and flags that no EV-specific mission has been encountered yet, both of which may change later in the story. The article's promotional EnergySage solar advertisement is excluded from this summary.
items.title: Electric Vehicles Portrayed as Mainstream in GTA 6's Vice City

items.summary:
A European hydrogen assessment by TFIE argues that industrial buyers set the price ceiling for hydrogen, and modelled supply costs exceed those ceilings across most applications. In its central 2050 scenario, on-site production reaches €5.70/kg from electricity at €60/MWh (€3.18/kg) plus electrolysers, capital recovery, maintenance, stack replacements, water and other plant costs; delivery can push this to €6.95/kg under a generic allowance or €5.81/kg for the hub-and-pipeline case. For process heat at 94% efficiency, one MWh of useful heat requires roughly 31.9 kg (about €182/MWh before burner and equipment costs), while direct-electric heating sets a competitive ceiling of only €2.07/kg—leaving hydrogen production €3.63/kg above the customer's affordable input price. The author treats this mismatch as the commercial test investors should apply, noting that reducing production cost from €7 to €5 is meaningless if customers can pay just €2.

The International Energy Agency's Global Hydrogen Review 2026 reaches a similar conclusion across most sectors and regions, finding maximum acceptable prices below US$2/kg without policy support and some incumbent-steel comparisons yielding negative values; the author notes the IEA uses a 2035 horizon and different competitors. TFIE's own assessment calculates ceilings for industrial heat (€1.43/kg against electrochemical iron), ammonia (green European ammonia competes with imports only when hydrogen costs roughly €2.62–€4.00/kg) and ironmaking (ceiling of €2.28 to €4.45/kg versus imported reduced or hot-briquetted iron, but about €1.43/kg against electrochemical iron). The author distinguishes chemical reagent use from heat use because burning hydrogen adds conversion losses and fuel-system costs.

The analysis is limited by its own stated boundaries: the supply cases are different cost structures rather than interchangeable quotes (€5.70/kg central onsite, €6.95/kg with delivery allowance, €5.81/kg hub-and-pipeline), even the favourable 2050 case at €3.46/kg clears some thresholds but misses others, and policy instruments such as carbon pricing, procurement mandates, subsidies and carbon contracts for difference can create demand that market prices do not support—though governments should disclose premiums rather than describe regulated purchases as competitive.

ACER reported 4.2 GW of committed electrolyser capacity in November 2026 (operating plants, projects under construction and those with final investment decisions), roughly 49% associated with refining where renewable-fuel mandates provide a demand signal; the remaining industrial sectors face a harder test without comparable policy compulsion. For lenders, TFIE concludes that a €5/kg plant has no viable commercial case when its buyer can afford €3/kg, and developers need enforceable contracts at prices covering supply costs or durable support to finance the difference.
items.title: TFIE's €5.70/kg Modelled Hydrogen Exceeds Industrial Buyers' Price Ceilings

items.summary: Earlier this week, Jackery announced a partnership with Brooklyn-based energy aggregator Every Electric to offer the first plug-in Virtual Power Plant (VPP), initially targeting New York City apartment residents. The program lets households earn money by turning household appliances into grid-stabilizing assets without feeding electricity back into the grid, which simplifies installation and requires no electrician or home electrical upgrades. Customers sign up with a refundable $30 deposit for priority or choose an option with no deposit while keeping their existing utility plan; they receive batteries free of charge, plug them into standard outlets, connect air conditioners to the batteries, and link the units to Wi-Fi. Users pay nothing out of pocket and can earn up to $150 per year per battery through active demand response—Every Electric describes this as 'Get paid to plug in.' Alternatively, customers may purchase a discounted battery for $650 with a higher annual payback of up to $250 per battery; over the 11-year rated lifespan, buying could increase total net payback despite higher upfront cost. Behind the scenes, Every Electric automates power management—charging when demand is low and discharging to run air conditioners during high-demand periods—and aggregates data across thousands of batteries sold to Con Edison, with benefits distributed to customers based on their contributions. Over 2,000 batteries were in the initial trial phase, with a larger rollout planned for next year; the author reports being on a waitlist alongside more than 15,000 other NYC households.
items.title: Jackery and Every Electric Launch a Plug-In Virtual Power Plant for NYC Apartment Residents

items.summary: Prof Heather Wardle, whose 20-year research documents the harms caused by gambling, discovered that her reputation and photograph were being used by illegal UK casinos to falsely claim she endorsed their games. Evidence reviewed by the Guardian indicates at least six prominent academics have had their identities misappropriated across almost 30 casino websites, most appearing to be affiliate businesses earning commission from directing traffic toward unlicensed operators not on GamStop. The misuse extends beyond academia: Jonathan Harbourne of the LGBT History Project identified about 40 other sites—including a hospital trust, an Italian restaurant in Croydon, and Sigma Research at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine—whose previously unrelated web addresses were bought cheaply after expiry to exploit existing search engine recognition. Of the 28 academic-name websites reviewed, most appeared registered in Ukraine; one site gave conflicting ownership claims across Malta, a UK Gambling Commission licence (which appears untrue), and Sydney, Australia. DomainLore auctioned many of these expired domains but stated it could not police their use after sale, while Nominet handles the underlying domain registrations. The Guardian found that none of the casinos it viewed held a UK operating licence. In response to the broader illicit market, which the Betting and Gaming Council estimates will see £33bn wagered by 2028, the government has provided the Gambling Commission with £26m over three years; in the first six months this year alone, the regulator issued more than 1,000 cease and desist letters, disrupted or geo-blocked 1,688 websites, referred more than 2,000 to search engines for delisting, and suspended 140 domains since July following Gambling Commission requests. New powers under the Crime and Policing Act 2026 are expected by year-end but their effectiveness remains unclear.
items.title: UK Academics and Organizations Have Their Identities Hijacked by Rogue Online Casinos

items.summary:
Westminster MP Sir Andrew Mitchell criticised plans by the governments of Guernsey and Jersey to allow approved applicants access to information about who owns or controls companies, saying they "do not go nearly far enough." The proposals follow a December 2023 joint commitment made by Guernsey, Jersey, and the Isle of Man to increase transparency around company ownership in tackling money laundering, terrorist financing, and other financial crime. Currently, beneficial-ownership information is generally available only to law enforcement agencies, regulators, and regulated businesses conducting anti-money-laundering checks; the new plans would extend access to journalists, academics, and others with a legitimate interest.

Mitchell argued that limits on access could leave national security threats "entirely invisible" to investigators. He said applicants being required to demonstrate they had been unable to find information elsewhere created a "catch-22," since investigators may need the register to prove wrongdoing in the first place, and described this requirement as defeating the object of a register. Jersey's consultation response states that applicants would be expected to show all reasonable alternative sources have been exhausted before access is granted; Guernsey's published response does not explicitly set out the same requirement. Mitchell also said access should be open to people from other jurisdictions, including those in "the global south," and argued information should be free at point of access rather than requiring payment.

Both governments rejected the criticism as inaccurate. A Government of Jersey spokesperson said its concerns did not reflect the consultation response paper and that the policy was intended to meet international commitments while maintaining a fair, proportionate framework, adding that Jersey continues to meet international standards for transparency and countering money laundering, terrorist financing, and proliferation financing. Deputy Andrew Niles of Guernsey's Policy & Resources Committee said Guernsey does not accept its proposals fall short or that it fails to meet international standards, noting the framework is based on a model adopted in the EU and would protect privacy while providing access for those with a legitimate interest in investigating crime.
items.title: MP Criticises Guernsey and Jersey Company Ownership Register Plans

items.summary: Paolo Bulgari, chairman of the Bvlgari Group since 1984 and a leading expert in gemstones who helped transform his family's business into a global luxury brand, has died in Rome aged 89. The company was founded by his grandfather, Greek silversmith Sotirios Voulgaris (who later adopted the name Bulgari), in Rome in the late 19th century after fleeing Ottoman rule from Paramythia in Epirus; Paolo joined shortly after leaving school and began collaborating with his father in 1960. The brand established a distinctive aesthetic favouring bold gemstones, rich yellow gold, generous proportions, and unexpected colour combinations rather than the delicate style associated with Parisian houses, earning clients among Hollywood stars such as Elizabeth Taylor, Audrey Hepburn, Marilyn Monroe, Ingrid Bergman, Sophia Loren, Anne Hathaway, Zendaya, and Rihanna. The business diversified beyond jewellery into watches, perfumes, leather goods, and hotels, and in 2011 the family sold its controlling stake to LVMH for approximately €3.7 billion; Paolo and his wife established the Paolo Bulgari Foundation in 2019 to support young people through schooling and job training in disadvantaged neighbourhoods on Rome's outskirts. The Bvlgari Group posted tributes describing him as 'the greatest jeweller of our time' and a creative soul whose legacy would continue to inspire future generations, while his funeral is scheduled for Monday, 23 November at the Basilica of Santa Croce in Gerusalemme in Rome.
items.title: Italian Jeweller and Businessman Paolo Bulgari Dies Aged 89

items.summary: As the 27 November Black Friday shopping period approaches, cybersecurity firms are warning that criminals are increasingly using artificial intelligence to create 'fake storefronts'—clones of legitimate brand websites designed to steal money or card details from bargain hunters. These sites typically appear as normal search results and can also surface in AI chatbot responses; National Trading Standards says criminals are 'pooning' AI models like ChatGPT so they recommend scam sites, while Guardio's Michael Vainshtein explains this is achieved through fake shopfronts and phishing pages that reach users via populated search results, Google ads, compromised sites, and social posts promoting hot sales. Norton expects suspect site numbers to rise significantly during the Black Friday-to-Christmas period, with security researcher Luis Corrons noting the annual increase between these dates; Leyla Bilge adds that young people are especially vulnerable because they encounter scams more often on social media and act on impulse, advising shoppers to treat a hard-to-find item suddenly appearing cheap from an unknown seller as a warning sign. The Guardian previously documented June examples of cloned sites mimicking Russell & Bromley with deceptive URLs such as therussellbromleyofficial and russellbromleyonlineuk. These AI-created clones often display identical branding, offer steep discounts like 80% off, use convincingly similar web addresses, and steer buyers toward bank transfers or cryptocurrency rather than card payments—sometimes pushing the PayPal 'send to a friend' option under the guise of avoiding fees. Consumers are advised to examine the URL (legitimate UK sites typically end in .co.uk or .com), watch for suspicious title words like 'official' or 'deals', and treat bank-transfer-only payment as an immediate red flag; tools such as The Co-operative Bank's safety checker can help assess suspicious content, while victims should report financial details to their bank and Report Fraud. All claims in this summary are attributed directly to the cited sources (Norton, National Trading Standards, Guardio), which represent expert opinion rather than verified incident data.
items.title: Cybersecurity Firms Warn of Surge in AI-Generated Black Friday Clone Websites

items.summary: Using Danish administrative data, Elin Colmsjö, Francesco Ruggieri, and Matteo Saccarola compared parents whose only child experienced a stroke at the same age but differed by the child's gender. Before the event, these parent groups followed similar health trajectories with comparable pre-existing conditions and healthcare utilization. After the stroke, a survival gap emerged that widened over time: five years later, parents of daughters were 1.5 percentage points more likely to be alive than parents of sons. Alongside this mortality difference, daughters adjusted more substantially across several margins—becoming more likely to live near their parents, less likely to remain married, and having fewer children—which the authors interpret as greater involvement in informal caregiving. Notably, parents of daughters used more physical rehabilitation, an elective form of formal care requiring sustained engagement; rather than displacing professional services, these daughters appeared more likely to help their parents access and use them. The study therefore suggests that informal and formal care can function at least partly as complements when responding to severe health shocks. A limitation is that the comparison relies on only children who differ solely in gender, so unobserved factors correlated with child sex could still confound the results.
items.title: Parents of daughters survive longer after a child's stroke in Denmark

items.summary: Following Prime Minister Narendra Modi's earlier advice to Indians to avoid buying gold, the Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) issued a letter dated November 22 crediting his warning with helping jewellers, small traders, and investors avoid heavy losses as gold prices declined sharply. The CTI stated that its members had been able to refrain from purchasing gold at elevated prices, potentially avoiding losses of ₹65 lakh per kg. This public acknowledgment came months after Modi's advice drew criticism. The account relies entirely on the CTI's own assessment; independent verification of the claimed loss figures or a direct causal link between the advice and avoided purchases is not established in this text.
items.title: Traders Credit PM Modi's Gold Warning After Prices Fall

items.summary: Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, and Yash, crossed ₹1,600 crore worldwide in 17 days, earning ₹1,616.70 crore globally including ₹906.90 crore net in India, making it the third-fastest Indian film to reach that domestic milestone. The film's box office run received a notable boost on its third Saturday with ₹27.40 crore net across all languages in India, per trade tracker Sacnilk—a 74 percent jump from the ₹15.75 crore collected Friday. No limitations or caveats were stated beyond attributing these figures to Sacnilk.
items.title: Ranbir Kapoor–Sai Pallavi, Yash's Ramayana: Rise of a Legend Crosses ₹1,600 Crore Worldwide and Becomes India's Third-Fastest Film to Reach ₹900 Crore

items.summary: Storms fueled by a super El Niño are battering the California coast, with scientists warning that rising sea levels and 'king tides' pose significant damage risks. On Thursday morning, the National Weather Service reported rainfall rates exceeding 25.4 mm per hour along the coast and issued multiple flash flood warnings; coastal trails around Point Vicente and Pelican Cove Park in Rancho Palos Verdes remained closed after heavy rains. An atmospheric river caused flooding in San Francisco on Wednesday, dumping about 67 mm of rain in one day—surpassing a record for that date set over a century ago—and left more than 51,000 electricity customers without power by the afternoon. El Niño raises sea levels along the U.S. West Coast, allowing high tides and powerful waves to reach farther inland; large swells continued hitting Southern California on Thursday, worsening erosion at sites including Crystal Cove State Park, where a 110-meter crack appeared in a coastal bluff beneath Pacific Coast Highway in October. The true test is expected next week: NOAA estimates roughly a 60% probability of a 'historic' El Niño for October through December that would exceed every event since records began in 1950. Starting Monday, coastal water levels in parts of Southern California could reach up to 2.4 meters during king tides running from Sunday through November 27; the California Coastal Commission says its season's highest tides won't occur until November 24-26, December 23-25, and January 21-22. In response, Governor Gavin Newsom signed an executive order on October 27 establishing a Highway 1 Task Force to identify vulnerable sections of the coastal highway; emergency project expenditures along Big Sur totaled about $312 million from 2020 through 2026.
items.title: El Niño-driven storms and king tides threaten California's coastline

items.summary:
At the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, economies adopted a statement titled 'Harnessing Digital and Emerging Technologies for Employment and Prosperity in the Asia-Pacific Region,' which links industrial upgrading with workforce development and worker protection. The document calls for using digital technologies to drive innovation, improve productivity, and support high-quality full employment across sectors including energy, agriculture, education, transportation, healthcare, and micro-, small- and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). It also emphasizes helping workers adapt through improved digital access and literacy, expanded vocational training, better-matched job-seeking services, and protections for worker rights, working conditions, and occupational safety. The APEC Human Resource Development Working Group is designated to coordinate implementation with other relevant bodies.

Experts offered interpretations rather than official endorsements: Jiang Tianjiao of Fudan University's Development Institute suggested APEC could help bridge the AI divide through open technologies, shared application scenarios, and joint risk management; Alejandro Reyes of the University of Hong Kong stressed that technology access alone is insufficient without effective use, cooperation on computing resources, language-specific models, and worker training—particularly in developing economies. The text notes these are expert perspectives rather than adopted positions.

The article contains no stated limitations or caveats beyond attributing analytical claims to their respective experts.
items.title: APEC Adopts Statement on Harnessing Digital Technologies for Employment in Asia-Pacific

items.summary: Negotiators at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) concluded a late-night closing plenary around midnight on Friday, November 21, 2026, in Antalya, Türkiye, with the final outcome document anticipated to be released over the weekend. COP31 President Murat Kurum stated that "very little distance remains" and urged delegations to prioritize consensus over individual priorities, expressing hope for an "Antalya Consensus." Negotiations Chair Chris Bowen added on Friday that parties would continue working "for as long as it takes," citing a "spirit of goodwill" among delegations. The latest draft texts centered on climate finance, adaptation support, clean energy, electrification, and carbon capture. COP31 opened November 9 with representatives from nearly 200 parties focused on delivering on climate pledges.
items.title: COP31 closing session ends in Antalya with outcome document expected over the weekend

items.summary: Following his November 20 trip to the APEC meeting in Shenzhen, U.S. President Donald Trump stated at a White House event that some American cities are "so embarrassing" compared with those in China. He characterized Chinese streets as clean and praised its infrastructure—roads, roadsides, and overall condition—as "flawless," attributing this development to Chinese President Xi Jinping. In contrast, Trump criticized the state of major U.S. cities, citing potholes, deteriorating infrastructure, and crime. The report is published by CGTN Now as part of a promotional feature encouraging subscriptions to its newsletter, The China Report; no independent verification or supporting data beyond these claims are provided in the text.
items.title: Trump Calls US Cities 'Embarrassing' Compared to Those in China

items.summary: Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham said Friday's UK-EU agreements on trade, travel, emissions and youth visas represent the first steps toward rebuilding relations after Brexit, though he stressed all options remain open. Ex-PM Theresa May countered that Britain should accept its 2019 vote as final and "move on," warning in a BBC interview about the enormous effort required for further negotiations with the bloc's 27 nations. The debate followed Friday's Brussels summit deals: allowing 100,000 young adults from each side to live and work in the other country for up to three years; scrapping border checks on plant and animal products, which Burnham said would lower food costs; and linking emissions trading schemes to reduce carbon taxes on some exports. On the price question, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband cited supermarket chains Morrisons, Co-op and Marks & Spencer as welcoming the red-tape cuts with downward pressure on prices, while noting that UK food exports have fallen 20% since Brexit due to regulatory burden; he declined to provide a specific figure or item for cheaper goods. The British Retail Consortium offered a more cautious view, saying the deals would reduce trading costs but are unlikely to affect consumer prices soon because most food already comes from within the UK. Critic Alex Burghart argued that removing red tape is bad for business since some farmers must follow EU regulations without trading with the bloc, and warned linking emissions schemes forces higher carbon pricing while a 100,000-place youth mobility scheme could take jobs from young Brits; Gove rebutted by saying nearly every supermarket CEO supports the deal. A further negotiation on university fees for European students in both countries is set to be resolved within six months.
items.title: UK Leaders Debate EU Trade Deals After Burnham Calls for Rebuilding Post-Brexit Ties

items.summary: South Korea's Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned on Sunday, taking full responsibility for last-minute measures aimed at preventing AI-assisted cheating during Thursday's annual college entrance exam, the Suneung. The resignation followed a week earlier when Han Won-seok, the top scorer in April's national tax accountancy exam with just one of 160 questions wrong, admitted using a microcamera to photograph test questions and sending them to an AI before checking answers on his smartphone. His confession prompted officials to introduce emergency anti-cheating measures days before the Suneung, including deploying South Korea's national disaster alert system for the first time—sending three nationwide alerts between 08:00 and 15:00 local time that triggered phones across the country regardless of silent mode or data roaming. Candidates were also required to cover buttons on their clothing and submit to eyewear inspections, prompting some honest test takers to wear contact lenses instead of glasses to avoid suspicion. The Suneung lasts up to nine hours and is taken by roughly 500,000 students. After the exam concluded, the education ministry reported that 111 candidates were found with unauthorized smart devices during this year's exam. President Lee Jae Myung—who has called for an overhaul of the current exam system—accepted Choi's resignation later on Sunday.
items.title: South Korea Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin Resigns Over AI-Assisted Cheating Scandal at Suneung

items.summary: The Indian Youth Congress, the youth wing of the main opposition Congress party, warned it would "storm your offices across the country and stage protests" unless Instagram accounts belonging to its leaders were restored. The warning came a day after protesters stormed into Meta's Hyderabad office on Friday, smashing plants and clashing with police in footage released by the group's X account; similar unrest occurred at Meta's Mumbai office and in Gurugram near New Delhi. Two of the youth wing's leader accounts had been restored following Friday's protests, but Manu Jain, who handles social media for the group, told Reuters that thousands of accounts belonging to journalists, creators, and influencers critical of the government remained restricted as of Saturday. He called on Meta to explain how its algorithms restrict posts and to restore accounts removed under government orders. India is Meta's largest market by users, though the company declined to comment on Friday's demonstrations; Congress has long accused platforms of suppressing dissent online while Modi's government says it only demands takedowns for content breaching local laws or threatening public safety or national security. The broader debate centers on free-speech risks from increasingly strict efforts to remove objectionable social media content, compounded by a February rule requiring companies to act within three hours—tightened from an earlier 36-hour timeline—and a new government rule giving platforms little time to review takedown requests; Reporters Without Borders noted that removal of journalistic content has been rising in India this year. Meta disclosures show it restricted more than 5.4 million posts or accounts in India under local laws in the first half of 2026, second only to Indonesia and up from about 70,000 across all of 2025, though Meta said most were cases where it was obligated to proactively restrict content based on local law requirements. The article notes that Congress criticized its own workers over vandalism at the Hyderabad office, and India's IT ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
items.title: Indian opposition party's youth wing warns of more Meta protests after police clashes

items.summary:
At the November 22, 2024 Las Vegas Grand Prix, Ferrari principal Fred Vasseur publicly condemned a collision between teammates Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton as "completely unacceptable." The incident followed an earlier clash between the two drivers at Mexico City, after which Ferrari held talks with both to prevent recurrence. Vasseur expressed frustration that the same mistake occurred despite prior discussions in Brazil and again during this weekend's race.

During the event, Leclerc attempted to overtake Hamilton on the inside in the latter stages of the race; contact spun Hamilton around. Stewards penalized Leclerc with a 10-second penalty for the incident, resulting in his tenth-place finish. Hamilton finished seventh after separately receiving a lap-12 penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage while passing McLaren's Lando Norris—a sanction he called "really harsh" and said cost him what could have been a podium given the car's pace.

Leclerc accepted responsibility, noting that stewards had determined his error was to blame. Hamilton declined to discuss the collision directly with Leclerc but acknowledged Ferrari faced internal challenges in their racing relationship while competing against McLaren for constructors' standings. When asked whether firmer team rules were needed, Hamilton deferred the decision entirely to Ferrari.
items.title: Ferrari Principal Condemns Leclerc-Hamilton Collision at Las Vegas Grand Prix

items.summary: Sunday marked the third consecutive day of protests across Europe, following demonstrations on Friday and Saturday from Portugal to France. The unrest has centered primarily on rising living costs and access to affordable housing. In France specifically, demonstrations have occurred for six weekends in a row. The source text provides no further detail on protest scale, participant numbers, or specific policy demands beyond these cost-of-living themes.
items.title: Protests Continue Across Europe Over Cost of Living

items.summary: In Yamaguchi Prefecture, a 37-year-old Russian national identified only as Roxy held her legal right to reside in Japan entirely through a marriage certificate. For four years she lived with and taught English while married to a Japanese husband. When the couple divorced in September, she lost her spouse visa; after immigration denied an application to switch to another status of residence, authorities voided her residence card and ordered her departure from the country. The case illustrates one estimate that roughly 128,000 foreign residents across Japan depend on marriage for their legal right to remain.
items.title: Foreign Spouse Visa Holders Face Deportation After Divorce in Japan

items.summary: At the Las Vegas Grand Prix on November 21, McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri finished second and third behind race winner Max Verstappen, marking a redemption for last year's double disqualification. Both drivers had started from pole position in 2025 but were disqualified after finishing second (Norris) and fourth (Piastri) due to excessive skid plank wear; Norris described that incident as an unfortunate 'freak thing' that did not benefit McLaren, while Piastri joked about saving his celebrations until final technical checks passed. The pair cautioned they would not fully solidify their happiness until scrutineering confirmed compliance with regulations. In the broader championship context reported by the article, McLaren finished fourth in the constructors' standings this season—nine points behind third-place Red Bull—and Mercedes has already secured both the drivers' and constructors' titles; Norris sits fifth on identical points to George Russell of Mercedes, while Piastri is seventh.
items.title: McLaren Drivers Celebrate Las Vegas Podium After 2025 Disqualification

items.summary: The Philippines, holding the 2026 ASEAN presidency and intending to conclude a code of conduct with China for the South China Sea during its term, abandoned that goal after an in-person summit in Manila in mid-November. According to Philippine Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro, roughly 80% of the text had been negotiated, but key areas of dispute remained unresolved. The stakes extend beyond diplomatic wording: the sea is a major global shipping route with valuable fishing grounds and potential oil and gas reserves, and China's Nine-Dash Line claims overlap those of the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, and Brunei. A code of conduct would set rules to prevent incidents at sea from escalating, but parties disagree on its binding nature and geographic scope.
items.title: Philippines Abandons Goal of South China Sea Code of Conduct at Mid-November ASEAN Summit

items.summary: A Japanese law introducing a Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS)-style system that checks for criminal records of sex offenses among people whose work involves contact with children is scheduled to take effect on December 25. The system requires schools—elementary, junior high, and high—and licensed nursery centers and child welfare institutions to participate, while participation by cram schools, sports clubs, and similar organizations remains voluntary but can earn government certification if operators meet requirements. Business operators may request the Justice Ministry, through the Children and Families Agency, to check whether an individual has a record for offenses such as nonconsensual sexual intercourse, child sexual exploitation, and voyeurism; a confirmed record leads to reassignment of existing employees away from children or withdrawal of job offers to prospective ones. The law also mandates preventive measures against first-time sexual violence, including defining inappropriate conduct—such as being alone with a child, private social-media communication, and unnecessary physical contact—and requiring consultation services and employee training. About 2.8 million people nationwide are expected to be covered by the program. Separately, the Children and Families Agency announced a delay in launching a national criminal-record-check system after discovering a vulnerability; an alternative procedure involving written-document exchange will be issued in early December. The education ministry reported that 281 public school teachers received disciplinary or administrative action for sex crimes or sexual misconduct in fiscal 2024, down 39 from the record high in fiscal 2023. Lawyer Kei Hida said the new system should help children and parents feel secure but stressed the need to explain its purpose and mechanisms and build shared workplace understanding of what constitutes sexual violence.
items.title: Japan's child-contact sex-offense record-check system set to launch Dec. 25, with separate national criminal-record check delayed

items.summary: Organized by Portugal's main trade union confederation, CGTP, a nationwide demonstration filled the capital's avenues with workers carrying umbrellas and banners who chanted for higher wages and better pensions while denouncing what they described as rising household expenses outpacing salaries. Placards emphasizing that 'everything increases except salaries' underscored concerns about housing, food, energy, and fuel prices, with affordability of housing—specifically rising rents making basic expenses difficult to cover—identified as a central issue. The protest occurred ahead of the final parliamentary debate on Portugal's 2027 budget, which was scheduled for vote on Tuesday, November 24, and unions announced further protests intended to increase pressure on the government over wages, pensions, and living standards.
items.title: Portuguese Workers Protest Ahead of Budget Debate Over Wages and Living Costs

items.summary:
Foreign Minister Penny Wong is set to deliver a major foreign policy speech in parliament on Tuesday, elevating artificial intelligence as a 'major foreign policy and national security challenge.' The address, titled 'Securing Australia's future in a changing world,' warns that AI gives foreign actors new tools for faster, cheaper, and harder-to-detect interference in Australian democracy. Wong cited reports of an Iranian operation using fake journalist personas to influence opinion on the US-Iran conflict, as well as Russian covert operations employing AI-generated deepfakes to affect US elections. She argued Australia cannot wait for international treaties and must act quickly amid rapid technological development while working with partners on safety standards.

The speech coincides with warnings from ASIO director general Mike Burgess that foreign adversaries could seek covert control over Australian AI data centres 'for nefarious reasons,' a statement made during his 60 Minutes interview. Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke acknowledged the national security interest in building domestic data centres, cautioning that onshore capability becomes attractive to those seeking foreign interference and stressing vigilance around ownership structures.

The timing follows US President Donald Trump's warnings of 'tremendous' consequences for American tech companies building AI infrastructure overseas. Separately, ASIO director general Burgess has been involved in reports concerning Jensen Huang of Nvidia amid allegations he was having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

Wong indicated Australia aims to shape the international order on AI as it did with nuclear proliferation and online safety, echoing Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's September UN call for global cooperation. Over the weekend, Australia and China agreed to hold talks following Albanese's APEC summit visit. The speech effectively replaces the foreign policy white paper concept, which Wong previously said becomes outdated quickly; the last such document was published in 2017.

The article presents these statements as planned remarks from an upcoming speech rather than confirmed positions, and reflects reporting on allegations without independently verifying them.
items.title: Australia Elevates AI as National Security Priority Ahead of Foreign Minister's Parliamentary Speech

items.summary: A fire broke out Saturday evening at the three-story PT Fonusa Agung Mulia confectionery factory in Cikande, Serang regency of Indonesia's Banten province, killing at least three workers and leaving 36 others unaccounted for. The blaze began around 5pm local time; a company representative said approximately 300 workers were inside when it started. Of the initial 54 missing, 15 have since been rescued, including four injured workers per the National Search and Rescue Agency. The remains of three killed workers were transferred to a hospital in black body bags because fire intensity rendered them unidentifiable by visual inspection, prompting DNA collection efforts from relatives and personal belongings. Survivors reported that the fire originated from a cooling unit on the third floor, though authorities had not confirmed the cause. Firefighters deployed 15 water-cannon-equipped trucks more than 12 hours after ignition; Tubagus Mahfud of the Serang fire department said hotspots remained in central and rear sections and warned production materials could allow reignition until cooling operations complete. A joint rescue team coordinated with families and the company to locate employees believed inside, while relatives waited outside the burned structure. The factory produces Milkita candies under United Family Food, which employs about 5,000 people nationwide.
items.title: Fire at PT Fonusa Agung Mulia Confectionery Factory in Banten Kills Three, Leaves 36 Workers Missing

items.summary:
A reported breach of the Federal Bureau of Investigation's National Crime Information Center (NCIC) database, which contains criminal history records on fugitives, missing persons, and stolen property, prompted President Donald Trump to characterize the incident as "not good" while suggesting it could yield benefits by exposing alleged voter fraud. The FBI launched an investigation into the breach earlier in the week.

The reported hack occurred within a broader wave of US technology outages affecting travel, communications, banking systems, and an internal National Security Agency system. Amid these mounting cybersecurity issues, national cyber director Sean Cairncross was removed from his position; Trump stated on Friday that he "didn't think that person was good enough." The role involves advising the president on cybersecurity policy, including information security, data protection, and deterrence of malicious activity.

Trump's comments referenced prior controversies, including what he termed a "Russia hoax," a "Ukraine hoax," and alleged voter fraud. Trump noted his tendency to frame situations positively, stating, "I always like to put things in a positive spin."
items.title: Trump Responds to Reported FBI NCIC Breach Amid Wave of US Tech Outages

items.summary: In Rwanda, 98% of women gave birth in a health facility as of 2025, but little attention has been paid to the quality of care these mothers receive. A nurse-midwife educator and researcher reported on a study by their colleagues that surveyed 246 mothers shortly after they delivered at a public hospital in Kigali, asking them how they were treated during labour or childbirth. Seven in ten respondents said they experienced at least one form of disrespect, defined to include insults or physical violence, being left alone when help was needed, treatment without dignity, and not being told what was happening. The most frequently reported experiences were abandonment (77 respondents) and undignified care (76 respondents), followed by 65 respondents who were not provided information about the care they received. A smaller number of women reported more serious incidents, including being beaten, pinched or kicked; having an episiotomy repaired without anaesthesia; or undergoing procedures without consent. The researchers noted that their findings reflect only one hospital and cautioned against blaming individual workers, pointing instead to systemic problems such as poor hygiene, inadequate infection prevention, shortages of supplies, overcrowding, and lack of trained psychological support staff.
items.title: Rwanda's near-universal facility births mask widespread disrespect during childbirth

items.summary: South Africa's child support grant supports over 13 million children in low-income households, terminating at the recipient's 18th birthday. Researchers from Stellenbosch University examined what happens to mental health when this support is withdrawn, given that more than half of young people aged 15-24 actively seeking work cannot find employment and losing R580 (US$35) a month can be a financial shock for struggling households. Using data from South Africa's National Income Dynamics Study covering 2010 to 2017, the team followed nearly 8,000 adolescents and young adults, comparing those within less than a year before their 18th birthday with those within less than a year after it to minimize statistical error. Depressive symptoms were measured using the Center for Epidemiologic Studies-Depression (CES-D) 10-item self-report scale. The study found a substantial increase in depressive symptoms when young people aged out of the grant, particularly pronounced immediately around the age threshold. Contributing factors included increased likelihood of job searching right after losing the grant—interpreted as pressure to compensate for lost income rather than improved opportunity—and effects being especially strong among poorer urban households and those with limited alternative income sources. The researchers noted their study cannot establish causation between increased job searching and mental health deterioration, though findings are consistent with young people responding to financial loss by seeking work in difficult circumstances.
items.title: Aging Out of South Africa's Child Support Grant Is Associated With Increased Depressive Symptoms

items.summary:
United Nations talks on regulating AI-powered lethal autonomous weapons systems ended Saturday with a weakened agreement to hold further discussions within two years, rather than adopting the binding rules sought by several parties. Approximately 100 countries supported regulation of weapons operating with little or no human oversight, but major arms-producing nations—including the United States, Russia, and Israel—opposed such measures.

UN High Representative for Disarmament Affairs Izumi Nakamitsu described the outcome as a "significant achievement" and emphasized that the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons remained significant amid rising conflict. She acknowledged the mixed nature of the result, noting Secretary-General António Guterres had sought a legally binding instrument negotiated and concluded before year's end—a commitment nations did not make—and expressed disappointment that states could not conduct an implementation review under the convention.

The week-long conference occurred against growing concern over lethal autonomous weapons use in Sudan, Ukraine, and the Middle East. Stop Killer Robots criticized the outcome as a "watered-down mandate," while Beatrice Fihn of Lex International characterized it as "pushing the can down the road for two more years." Advocacy groups attributed much of the obstruction to Russia and other leading AI-weapon developers seeking greater latitude.

Pope Leo XIV and numerous humanitarian organizations framed the issue existentially, urging swift action before such weapons become too widespread to regulate. Activists report that armed drones capable of independently striking targets have been deployed in some instances but not rolled out broadly.
items.title: UN Nations Agree to Delayed Talks on Regulating AI 'Killer Robots' and Drones

items.summary:
The Caine Prize for African Writing concluded after a month-long investigation that Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza's prize-winning short story, The Blue Fighter—which depicts a family's financial struggles following the father quitting his job to build fish tanks—was human-written. Kundizeza was announced as the winner of the $13,000 award on 6 October.

The allegations emerged days after an article in The Atlantic reported that AI-detection software called Pangram found the story to be almost entirely artificially generated; the program itself relies on AI. Kundizeza described the accusation as deeply troubling, saying it questioned his integrity and attributed work he did not create to a machine. He emphasized that the investigation adopted a human-centered approach rather than relying solely on what he characterized as inaccurate detection technology.

The Caine Prize stated the matter is now closed following an internal review involving rigorous interviews with Kundizeza and metadata analysis of drafts, allowing him to share details proving his authorship. The episode prompted broader social media debate about whether Black authors are disproportionately targeted by AI-related accusations; academic Dr Reggermore Marongedze argued that doubting a human's ability to produce brilliant work implicitly questions human intelligence and is used in racial contexts to discredit Black scholars.

The prize announced plans to celebrate Kundizeza in Zimbabwe before year-end and introduced new safeguards for future submissions, including AI declarations from publishers and shortlisted writers alongside an 'AI use policy for guidance.' The text presents these claims as reported statements without independent verification of the underlying investigation's findings.
items.title: Caine Prize Clears Zimbabwean Author of Using AI to Write Winning Story

items.summary:
Frank Tiberi, a 32-year-old Philadelphia saxophonist in the early 1960s, secretly recorded John Coltrane during live club performances to study and preserve his improvisational style. Between 1960 and 1964 he attended small venues where drinks cost a dollar and there was no cover charge, concealing a Concertone TR-100 Transicorder tape recorder under his coat with the microphone slipped beneath it; because each side held at most 30 minutes of music, he developed the skill of flipping the tape over blindly without removing the device. He accumulated 80 tapes containing roughly 26 hours of music and kept them hidden for about 60 years before showing them to touring musicians such as Joe Lovano and George Garzone.

The recordings were first digitized in early 2001 when Tiberi visited Verve Label Group offices carrying the boxes; Ken Druker oversaw transferring them from tape to CD at studios in Edison, New Jersey. A release was then abandoned because sound quality was insufficient for a CD-only market before vinyl's resurgence and streaming existed. Impulse/Universal released the material on November 6 around Coltrane's centenary (he was born September 23, 1926), with rights cleared by his widow Alice Coltrane and son Ravi Coltrane; engineers explored AI-based restoration but did not use it.

The edition includes a slower-tempo version of Giant Steps at about 228 bpm allowing a more melodic solo, plus audio of the movement Resolution from A Love Supreme recorded September 18, 1964 at Pep's in Philadelphia with Coltrane's canonical lineup (McCoy Tyner on piano, Elvin Jones on drums, Jimmy Garrison on bass) three months before the December 1964 studio session. Critics note the recordings are diffuse and muffled, occasionally capturing nearby conversations, which limits appreciation of spontaneous interaction among musicians; writer Mariano Peyrou says low frequencies from double bass, drums and piano remain inaudible.
items.title: 98-Year-Old Saxophonist Frank Tiberi's Secretly Recorded John Coltrane Performances Released by Impulse/Universal

items.summary: The Ette Ennaka, formerly known as the Chimila, are an Indigenous group in northern Colombia that nearly disappeared after colonial violence declared them extinct but has since regrouped to around 4,000 people across four reserves. On October 1, 2026, they attended a presentation of a bill by Senator Patricia Caicedo's Historic Pact movement intended to codify the Línea Negra (Black Line), a territory spanning roughly 573,000 hectares that requires consultation with Sierra Nevada Indigenous peoples before projects affecting them proceed. The Ette Ennaka criticized the bill for naming only four groups—the Kogui, Wiwa, Kankuamo, and Arhuaco—though Caicedo said the specific reference was not meant to exclude other communities but rather to strengthen existing legal foundations. Historically, the Línea Negra decree was formalized in 2018 under President Juan Manuel Santos as part of the FARC peace agreement, but a court challenge backed by mining and oil industry associations led Colombia's Council of State to strike it down in February 2026 on grounds that the Wayuu, Chimila, and Taganga communities had not been consulted. When then-President Gustavo Petro signed a new decree in May, the Ette Ennaka saw an opportunity to reclaim rights taken from them. The group lists demands including expansion of territory ordered by a land judge but not yet guaranteed, stronger food security, improved health care and education for their ethno-education project teaching their language ette taara, official recognition that seven Indigenous peoples inhabit the Sierra Nevada rather than four, consultation on projects affecting their reserves, and backing from other groups for recognizing a proposed Línea Blanca (White Line) mapping sacred sites. Before Spanish conquest, the greater Chimila nation occupied more than 10,810 square miles; today the Ette Ennaka hold about 9,840 acres—roughly 15 square miles—for some 500 families, with nearly half preserved for environmental protection and less territory than Colombian guidelines recommend for family agriculture. The four traditional peoples argue the Línea Negra reflects their own worldview but do not deny other groups' rights; Kogui representative Juangil Garavito said he would not oppose a Línea Blanca if used to defend territory rather than support mining or hydrocarbon activities. The group's prospects are complicated by right-wing President Abelardo de la Espriella, who took office in August 2026 and has pledged to promote mining and energy as economic drivers while reportedly seeking to repeal the Indigenous Territorial Entities framework that allows autonomous governance.
items.title: Ette Ennaka Indigenous Group Seeks Recognition and Consultation in Colombia's Sierra Nevada

items.summary: IIT Kharagpur announced on November 21, during its platinum jubilee celebrations, that Google has pledged $5 million to strengthen advanced artificial intelligence (AI) research, expand educational opportunities, and develop the next generation of technology professionals. IIT Kharagpur Director Suman Chakraborty told PTI that Sundar Pichai, a Google CEO and institute alumnus, played a key role in facilitating the funding. The pledge will primarily support applied AI research in areas including Indic languages, agriculture, materials science, and educational technology. According to Chakraborty, the grant is channeled through three broad areas: advanced AI research; educational opportunities, including expansion of AI training and curriculum for students and faculty; and capacity building through development of campus AI infrastructure, frameworks, and tools. He added that another alumnus, Jyoti Chatterjee, had separately pledged an additional $5 million as a seed endowment to develop a next-generation data initiative. The director said the contributions are expected to provide a major boost to the institute's efforts to expand AI-driven innovation and enhance its role in developing skilled technology professionals.
items.title: Google pledges $5 million to IIT Kharagpur for AI research

items.summary:
The Maharashtra Pollution Control Board issued a stop-work notice to the Adani Group over unauthorized excavation and construction at its pumped storage project in Satara district. An inspection conducted on 20 November found that excavation work and labour camps had been set up without environmental clearance or consent, alongside violations of air and water pollution norms at the Patan taluka site. As a result, all work was ordered to halt immediately, with warnings of strict legal action if construction continued without proper approvals.

The source text contains several unrelated news items that lack supporting evidence within the provided material: claims about gold prices dropping due to economic factors following Modi's comparison of gold-buying appeals to Shastri's austerity message; a Bihar political dispute involving PM Modi, Nitish Kumar, and Prashant Kishor over the inauguration of Nitish Setu; China revealing AI, robotics, and electric vehicle innovations in Guangzhou and Shenzhen ahead of an APEC conference; and the arrest of a suspect following CCTV footage from a train coach assault at Nagercoil railway station. These items are presented without verifiable detail or corroboration beyond their own assertions.
items.title: Maharashtra Pollution Control Board Halts Adani Group Construction in Satara

items.summary:
Lieutenant General Matthew Jones, head of UK defence intelligence, warned at the Cambridge intelligence seminar on Friday that Vladimir Putin's increasingly aggressive posture toward the West could produce a serious miscalculation with potentially catastrophic consequences. Jones stated he did not believe Moscow was actively seeking war with NATO but cautioned that Russia's reckless conduct raised the risk of an incident escalating into wider conflict, describing his greatest fear as precisely such a miscalculation and attributing Putin's assertiveness to pressure on him.

Jones cited numerous incidents involving Russian activity near or within NATO territory. He identified a drone attack at Leipzig airport in Germany as 'the most egregious recent example,' alongside the reported landing of two Russian missiles and a suspected drone over Poland, an alleged intelligence-linked plot to assassinate a US-Ukrainian citizen in Denmark, sinking merchant ships off Romania's Black Sea coast, a near shootdown of an RAF Rivet Joint aircraft over the Black Sea, a Russian-backed arson attack on a Ukrainian business in east London, and the 2018 Salisbury Novichok poisoning that killed Dawn Sturgess after she contacted discarded nerve agent.

Jones stressed that Britain does not seek conflict or confrontation with Russia but will 'robustly defend' national security when threatened. His remarks accompanied Defence Secretary Wes Streeting's statement that Britain must be ready for war by 2030, which Jones clarified was a preparation timeline rather than a prediction of imminent attack.

The warnings followed the thwarted assassination plot in Denmark and Poland's report of Russian missiles and a suspected drone landing on its territory. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband expressed solidarity with Denmark over the 'egregious attempted assassination,' while Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham called the Polish incident 'utterly unacceptable.' Jones framed these events as evidence that preparing for potential military threats is sensible, though he did not assert an attack was imminent.
items.title: UK Defence Intelligence Chief Warns Putin's Aggression Risks Escalation to World War III

items.summary: Anthropic launched its Nasdaq IPO on November 19, with the company's market value reaching nearly $1.3 trillion by the end of first-day trading; shares closed at $97.17, about 17% above the $83 offering price. At that offering price, CNBC estimated employee equity was worth roughly $232 billion on paper, or approximately $44 million per employee across a workforce of 5,300 people. Anthropic's prospectus listed outstanding options covering about 1.77 billion shares with a weighted-average exercise price of $2.91; at the offering price an option at that average was worth about $80 per share before taxes, while more than 1 billion restricted stock unit shares had not yet met vesting conditions. Investors told CNBC that at least 400 early employees could each hold equity worth $100 million or more, though the exact number of staff with holdings worth at least $1 million remained unclear. Redfin estimated current and former employee post-IPO equity wealth would be enough to buy 9% of San Francisco's homes, while brokers expect some employees to borrow against shares for property purchases; Anthropic also offers donation matching on vested shares based on hire date relative to May 17, 2024. The article notes that final amounts depend on sellable shares, sale prices and taxes, and that the number of millionaires is uncertain.
items.title: Anthropic's IPO made thousands of staff millionaires

items.summary:
Levent Alpöge, a researcher at Anthropic, published a note on his personal website claiming he used the company's Claude software to construct a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, a number theory problem concerning prime distribution that has resisted solution for over 150 years. He shared code written in Lean as supporting evidence and described reaching out to CEO Dario Amodei about publicizing the result; Alpöge characterized the timing as 'horrible' but stated he could not wait longer, while Anthropic declined to comment.

The claim would represent a second Millennium Prize Problem potentially solved by AI, following OpenAI's September report that its models generated a solution to the 90-year-old Navier-Stokes problem. Andrew Sutherland, a senior research scientist at MIT, verified Alpöge's work on his own computer and reported seeing at least three additional verifications across systems from other professional mathematicians; he described himself as both nervous and excited, noting that years of scrutiny remain before the proof can be fully understood or applied.

Noah Giansiracusa, an associate professor at Bentley University and faculty associate at Harvard, stated there is a 'pretty good chance this is airtight and valid.' Alpöge framed his contribution as building on decades of prior mathematical work and formalization efforts rather than originating the result independently. The claims remain unconfirmed pending further verification by the broader mathematics community.
items.title: Anthropic Researcher Claims AI-Assisted Proof of Riemann Hypothesis

items.summary: The FDA, Pune Division, suspended the food business licences of two quick-commerce dark stores operated by Amazon (Gajanan Inventories) and BigBasket (Innovative Retail Concept) on Sinhagad Road under the state government's 'Safe Food, Safe Drugs, Safe Maharashtra' campaign. The action was carried out on November 21 following surprise inspections that found expired food products—such as laddoos, pedhas, cakes, pav, milk rusk and chutney—at both facilities; pest infestation and inadequate pest control at each store; improper storage conditions including food placed directly on the floor, damaged flooring, unhygienic cold rooms, dust accumulation in containers, a broken ghee container lid, leaking oil from cartons and packets, and co-storage of food with non-food items like soap and ghee. Amazon's facility also lacked records relating to personnel hygiene and sanitation, while BigBasket's Bombay pav packet was missing mandatory manufacturing and use-by-date information. The violations breached Schedule IV of the Food Safety and Standards Act regarding storage and hygiene requirements. Enforcement officers included Food Safety Officer Supriya Jagtap under Joint Commissioner (Food) Shrikant Karkale with guidance from Assistant Commissioner (Food) Narayan Sarkate, who directed food businesses to comply strictly with licensing conditions or face suspension or cancellation. In a separate enforcement drive conducted between November 2 and 14 for violations of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940—including non-compliance with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and adulterated Ayurvedic products containing allopathic ingredients—the FDA suspended licences of five drug manufacturing units and seven medical stores. The affected establishments were Shivam Pharma in Hadapsar, Bharat Chemist on Dehu Road, Ganesha Medical in Khed, Shrutikaraj Medicals in Moshi, Lifeline Medico in Talegaon Dabhade, Arihant Medical and Morya Medical in Baramati; the manufacturing units were Jeevak Ayurvedic Pvt Ltd in Kolhapur, Alhad Ayurvedic Products in Shahapur, Ratnatray Ayur Pharma in Kasba Sangaon Kagal, Parco Pharmaceuticals in Nasrapur Bhor, and Punarvasu Ayurved in Sangli. Joint Commissioner (Drug) Girish Hukare noted that although drug manufacturing unit inspections are mandated every three years nationally, Maharashtra conducts them annually to ensure GMP compliance. Across the state during the same period, the drug department conducted 319 inspections covering 60 manufacturing units and 259 retail establishments, issued 137 notices, suspended or cancelled 114 licences (with 24 notices, 13 cancellations and five suspensions among manufacturers), and carried out six search and seizure operations confiscating drugs and cosmetics valued at approximately ₹2.28 crore.
items.title: FDA Pune Suspends Amazon and BigBasket Dark Store Licences Amid Food Safety Violations

items.summary:
The week's Indian primary-market activity centers on three mainboard IPO openings and two listings. Integris Medtech is preparing an issue estimated at Rs 3,000 crore; it had initially proposed raising Rs 925 crore through a fresh issue but reduced that figure to Rs 600 crore while also cutting the offer-for-sale (OFS) size, with the final amount dependent on the price fixed for existing shareholders' shares. Foodlink F&B Holdings will open its mainboard IPO on Thursday, November 26, closing subscription on Monday, November 30; it comprises a fresh issue of Rs 192 crore plus an OFS of up to 88.35 lakh equity shares by existing shareholders, with the price band still unannounced and final size pending that decision. Mahanadi Coalfields' Rs 8,981-crore IPO subscription window closed on Monday, November 23, ahead of its listing on Friday, November 27; the issue is entirely an OFS of 66.18 crore equity shares by parent Coal India, so the company will receive no proceeds from the public offering, with basis of allotment expected to be finalized on November 25 before BSE and NSE listings. Crystal Crop Protection's Rs 455.49-crore IPO closed on November 20 and is scheduled to list on November 26. In the SME segment, Shree Siddhivinayak Greentech Industries will launch its Rs 93.66-crore issue on Wednesday, November 25, open until Friday, November 27, with a price band of Rs 130-142 per share and listing proposed on the NSE SME platform.

The combined fundraising estimate for Integris Medtech and Foodlink F&B Holdings is stated at approximately Rs 3,300 crore but remains uncertain because both companies have not finalized pricing. Supporting financials are provided only for Foodlink: FY26 revenue of Rs 567.50 crore against a loss of Rs 16.15 crore on Rs 219.8 crore in the six months ended September 2026, with planned allocations of Rs 21.3 crore to a centralized kitchen and Rs 41.5 crore to two new banquets.

The article is authored by Podishetti Akash, who is not an SEBI-registered Research Analyst or Investment Adviser; the views are attributed to respective research analysts/brokerages rather than The Economic Times Digital, and readers are cautioned that final issue sizes depend on yet-to-be-announced price bands.
items.title: IPO Calendar: Rs 3,300 Crore in IPOs Lined Up for the Week

items.summary: Vatsal Bhuva, Technical and Derivative Research Analyst at LKP Securities, presented a weekly market strategy via an ETMarkets chat, projecting that the Nifty index could target 26,000 with potential upside to 26,500. He identified 26,000 as immediate psychological resistance—with sustained moves above it opening 26,500—and noted that prior resistance at 25,650 has converted into support. Bhuva advised a buy-on-dips approach rather than chasing the index, suggesting fresh long positions around 25,650 with a stop-loss of 25,400 and an initial target of 26,200, while flagging that November was Nifty's best month since 2020. He cited broadening participation in Nifty IT and Auto alongside strength from HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, and Reliance Industries as supportive factors, along with global AI/semiconductor corrections, crude oil around $90–93 per barrel, a recovering rupee, and sustained FII cash-market buying; he projected an elevated probability of the Nifty testing or surpassing its prior all-time high during December. For Bank Nifty—already at peak with a daily RSI near 83 indicating overbought conditions—he recommended avoiding fresh directional positions while letting existing longs ride to a trailing stop-loss at 63,800 and shifting focus to individual banking stocks such as Kotak Mahindra Bank, Axis Bank, SBI, Union Bank, and PNB. He characterized Kaynes Technologies' technical structure as weakened by an active double-top pattern and a breach of the ~3,350 (61.8% Fibonacci) support, advising against bottom-fishing while viewing any recovery toward 3,000 as a potential relief move; he also framed Nifty IT's correction as likely healthy retracement above its 31,200 support zone but warned that metals could stay volatile amid a strengthening US Dollar Index. His two stock picks were Tata Elxsi (entry 3,850–3,800, stop-loss 3,760, target 4,000) and Nykaa (around 364, stop-loss 352, target 380), each supported by technical recovery signals such as reclaimed moving averages and bullish RSI crossovers. The analysis rests entirely on Bhuva's unverified technical views; the text contains no confirmed price data or market results to validate these projections.
items.title: Vatsal Bhuva's Weekly Strategy: Buy-on-Dips on Nifty Toward 26,000–26,500 and Two Stock Picks

items.summary:
Indian sources reported on Sunday that claims India sought permission from Nepal to use the Bagdogra entry point in West Bengal for military aircraft are false. Citing reports attributed to ANI news agency, officials stated there is no such proposal and rejected suggestions that India had approached Nepal regarding military access.

The clarification emerged during broader discussions on air connectivity between the two countries ahead of Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah's state visit to India from November 22-23. While media reports indicated India was seeking airspace access for civilian flights operating to and from Bagdogra airport as part of reciprocal air connectivity talks, sources categorically denied any proposal concerning military aircraft.

Shah will arrive in New Delhi at the invitation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi for a two-day visit that marks his first trip abroad since assuming office in March 2026. The leaders are expected to hold bilateral talks on November 23 and review India-Nepal relations, with Nepal's ministry of foreign affairs confirming Shah would travel aboard a Nepal Airlines aircraft accompanied by finance minister Swarnim Wagle, foreign minister Shishir Khanal, and chief adviser Kumar Byanjankar.
items.title: India Denies Seeking Nepal Airspace for Military Flights Amid Bilateral Talks

items.summary:
A political confrontation unfolded on Saturday at the newly inaugurated Nitish Setu bridge in Vaishali, Bihar, when Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) workers pulled down National Democratic Alliance banners and posters hours after Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the structure. Social media videos showed a large RJD crowd tearing down displays while shouting slogans for party supremo Lalu Prasad Yadav and opposition leader Tejashwi Yadav; police moved alongside but appeared unable to control the gathering, according to reports. The BJP accused the RJD of politicizing an infrastructure project rather than acknowledging its benefits.

The six-lane Nitish Setu was inaugurated by Modi on November 21 at an estimated cost of Rs 4,280 crore and connects Kacchi Dargah with Bidupur, expected to improve north-south Bihar connectivity and reduce pressure on Mahatma Gandhi Setu. The bridge's naming has drawn separate criticism: Congress leader Pawan Khera questioned the decision to christen it after Nitish Kumar instead of Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru, arguing it hurt Sikh sentiments and possibly sidelined a living former chief minister; he shared a Bihar Road Construction Department document containing an RJD resolution on the proposed name. The Bihar Assembly later said no House decision had been taken for the Guru Gobind Singh naming.

AAP leaders in Punjab—Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema, Assembly speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan, and MLA Kuldeep Singh Dhaliwal—also urged reconsideration, citing the bridge's proximity to Takht Sri Patna Sahib. Tejashwi claimed Nitish Kumar had opened the bridge around 17 months earlier and challenged the BJP to identify its contribution.

The event also revived an election-season image: Modi waved his gamcha during the inauguration, recalling a similar gesture at a BJP office in Patna after the NDA won 202 of Bihar's 243 seats in the 2025 assembly elections. The inauguration was attended by governor Lt Gen Syed Ata Hasnain (retd), Union minister Chirag Paswan, chief minister Samrat Choudhary, and other dignitaries.
items.title: RJD Workers Tear Down NDA Banners Hours After PM Modi Inaugurates Nitish Setu in Bihar

items.summary:
According to the Henley & Partners Passport Index published on November 22, 2026, India ranked 84th among over 199 passports assessed globally, a decline of four positions from its January 2026 ranking of 80th. The index measures passport strength primarily by counting visa-free destinations accessible to holders without prior visas and weighing additional factors.

The drop occurred even though the number of countries granting Indian citizens visa-free access remained unchanged at 55, indicating that other variables influenced the country's revised position. Palak Gupta, an advocate with Jotwani Associates, attributed the decline to growing concerns among several countries regarding irregular migration, overstaying, security screening requirements, unauthorized employment, and asylum applications—factors prompting nations to reconsider previously liberal entry policies.

Gupta further noted that international mobility is increasingly governed by advance screening and electronic verification systems rather than relying solely on traditional visa procedures. She added that upcoming trade agreements may partially offset the weakened standing: the India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement, along with a negotiated framework under the India-European Union Free Trade deal, are expected to facilitate temporary movement for specified professionals and service suppliers.

The analysis is grounded entirely in claims made by Henley & Partners and Advocate Gupta. No independent verification of these figures or projections was provided within the source material.
items.title: India's Passport Strength Declines to 84th in Henley Index
