items.summary: A Qatari VIP jet operated by Qatar Amiri Flight landed sideways at Belp (Bern) Airport on Tuesday, November 17, after battling strong crosswinds during its descent from Doha as flight QAF9. The Airbus A320-214 touched down around 2:40 PM local time on the airport's 1,730-metre runway while weather reports recorded west-south-westerly winds of 12 to 16 knots with gusts up to 35 knots—roughly 65 kmph. To counter the crosswinds, pilots executed a crab approach by angling the nose into the wind before straightening it moments before touchdown. Aviation spotter Matthias Hänni, who filmed the descent for Swiss publication 20 Minuten, said he repeatedly expected the aircraft to abort its landing and climb back; airline pilot and National Council member Thomas Hurter likewise suggested a go-around would have been preferable under conditions that reportedly forced another government aircraft to abort around the same time. The clip circulated widely online after Al Arabiya English shared it, accumulating over 4.19 lakh views on YouTube, though Swiss media reports clarified that Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani was not aboard despite viewer speculation—the jet carried members of his delegation ahead of a two-day state visit to Switzerland scheduled for November 18 and 19.
items.title: Qatari Amiri Flight Jet Lands Sideways in Crosswinds at Bern Airport

items.summary: Russia's defense ministry reported overnight strikes on several targets, including the Pravoberezhna power plant in Zaporizhzhia, facilities at Kiliya port on the Danube River in the Odesa region, and a dry-cargo vessel northeast of Odesa; these claims could not be independently verified and Ukraine had not commented. Ukrenergo, Ukraine's grid operator, said weekend attacks caused severe damage to transmission-network infrastructure, making it physically impossible to deliver necessary electricity volumes to consumers in Odesa and the surrounding region. Separately, Ukraine's emergency services reported a Russian airstrike destroyed a five-story residential building and ignited a blaze in Dymer village in the Kyiv region, with residents evacuated but at least 14 possibly trapped under rubble. On drone activity, Ukraine's General Staff said forces launched 186 drones overnight—of which 161 were shot down—at 18 locations, with debris from downed UAVs found at six; Kursk region governor Alexander Khinshtein separately reported shooting down 150 drones and three injuries. Ukrainian forces conducted a large-scale strike on energy infrastructure in the self-proclaimed Donetsk People's Republic, causing widespread outages that left more than 279,000 people without power per Tass citing the region's head of government. The exchanges followed Saturday's drone attack on a Russian cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland and Russia's Friday air attacks against Ukraine.
items.title: Russia Strikes Ukrainian Energy Facilities as Power Supply Strains in Odesa Region

items.summary: At PPFAS Mutual Fund's 13th unitholders' meet, CIO and Director Rajeev Thakkar explained the fund house's continued exposure to IT services stocks despite negative market sentiment. The fund maintains less than 10% of its portfolio in IT services companies, citing recent employee additions and technology job openings as evidence that the sector is not becoming obsolete. Thakkar argued that exaggerated narratives should be evaluated against actual business developments rather than prevailing sentiment, noting that excessively unpopular sectors can create investment opportunities while market favorites risk excessive valuations and muted returns over several years.
items.title: PPFAS Mutual Fund's Rajeev Thakkar Defends IT Services Holdings Despite AI Concerns

items.summary: A 17-year-old girl in Kerala was diagnosed with membranous nephropathy, a serious autoimmune kidney condition that damages the glomeruli and can lead to further kidney complications if untreated. Nephrologist Gowri S at Aster MIMS Mother Hospital in Malappuram said she is being treated for the ailment. The girl reportedly ordered an online fairness cream after watching Instagram influencer videos claiming it could remove pimples, dark spots, and pigmentation; she initially found it effective and purchased several bottles over about one year through a WhatsApp number provided on Instagram. Medical examinations detected dangerously high mercury levels in her blood and body, which the doctor said can severely damage kidney filtering units. Tests conducted on the cream allegedly showed mercury at 12,500 parts per million (ppm), against India's permissible level of less than one ppm; Gowri S attributed the girl's kidney ailment to this mercury-containing product. The article explains that mercury is often added to fairness creams for rapid skin lightening but is banned as an active ingredient in cosmetics across India and several other countries, because it is highly toxic: when applied to skin, it enters the bloodstream, accumulates in the kidneys over time, and damages glomeruli and tubules before manifesting as severe kidney disease. The Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights registered a suo moto case following media reports and sought explanations from the Director of Health Services, the State Police Chief, the Drugs Controller, the Central Consumer Protection Authority, and the hospital superintendent. The girl's family has decided to sue the company in consumer court but has not disclosed the cream's name pending legal action; she alleged that after informing the company about her health problems it initially said officials would be informed before stopping all responses.
items.title: Kerala teen develops kidney disease after using mercury-laced fairness cream promoted by Instagram influencers

items.summary: Citizens and animal rights activists held a candlelight protest against the Greater Chennai Corporation, alleging mismanagement of animal birth control centres through botched surgeries and inadequate postoperative care that they say have caused cruelty and deaths among animals. The activists stated these complaints have persisted for about a decade across multiple administrations. They are demanding better regulation, fair inquiry, and transparency in how funds for animal welfare are used. The protest is presented as one item within a broader news roundup of unrelated events, including seat-sharing talks between the Samajwadi Party and Congress for Uttar Pradesh elections, political tension over a Supreme Court order on Karthigai Deepam lighting, Nepal's Prime Minister choosing India for his first overseas visit, and Maharashtra halting Adani Group construction at its Satara pumped storage project due to pollution breaches.
items.title: Candlelight Protest in Chennai Over Animal Birth Control Centre Mismanagement

items.summary: Congress leaders distanced themselves from party leader Imran Masood's allegation that Mohammed Siraj was excluded from India's test squad against New Zealand on the basis of religion rather than performance. Following public outcry over the omission, Masood suggested Friday that the decision reflected religious bias and later extended his claims to Mohammed Shami and Sarfaraz Khan, arguing selections should depend only on form regardless of a player's background. Congress leader Mumtaz Patel countered by saying squad selection is based on fitness and conditions rather than religion or state identity, warning against linking hate into cricket while blaming top political leaders for rising religious polarisation in society. Congress MP Ranjeet Ranjan urged Masood to keep politics separate from sports, citing merit as the sport's own criterion. Former cricketer Madan Lal also rejected the claims, stating Indian cricket has never discriminated on religious grounds and will not do so going forward. The BJP dismissed the allegations as vote-bank politics; Union minister Kiren Rijiju said opportunities are given on merit regardless of religion or caste, while national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari accused Congress of communalism in team selection. India's batting coach Sitanshu Kotak defended leaving Siraj out, saying management chose its best XI based on conditions at Wellington and that the decision was made for days two through four rather than day one.
items.title: Congress leaders reject Imran Masood's religious-bias claim over Siraj's Test exclusion

items.summary: Neera Chandhoke's book, Languages of Freedom: The Idea of India in Political Theory, Bombay Cinema and Progressive Urdu Poetry (Speaking Tiger Books), examines the concept of freedom through five essays that integrate Western political philosophy with the Indian perspective. Framing her analysis against Rousseau's assertion that humans are innately good but corrupted by society—leading to a trade of individual liberty for civil social liberty—the book explores how conflicting freedoms between individuals and society must be negotiated, including how poverty and illiteracy impose 'unfreedom.' The five essays address distinct aspects: Gandhi's concept of swaraj compared to utopian visions from Plato, Thomas More, and Leo Tolstoy; the tension between Indian and Western culture as reflected in thinkers like Aurobindo Ghosh and KC Bhattacharya, with emphasis on India's historical syncretism ('saanjhi virasat'); how Urdu poetry and Hindi cinema advanced secularism, equality, liberty, and fraternity from the 1930s to 1950s through organizations such as the Progressive Writers Association and Indian People's Theatre Association; and a comparison of Indian political philosophy with Western thought via figures like Rajaram Mohan Roy and Swami Vivekananda. The review characterizes the book as finely balanced between India and the West, theory and practical examples, and objective in its treatment—for instance, praising Gandhi's non-violence while criticizing his reliance on Hindu-derived ideas—though it notes that the second and fifth essays require careful reading due to their intensity, making them less accessible than sections drawing on popular culture. The review presents these assessments as subjective interpretations rather than established facts.
items.title: Review of Neera Chandhoke's 'Languages of Freedom': A Balanced Examination of Freedom Across Indian Political Theory, Literature, and Film

items.summary:
As of November 16 in the 2026-’27 agricultural season, Maharashtra recorded just 10.02 lakh hectares of Rabi sowing according to its Agriculture Department’s crop-wise and division-wise report—about 17% of the state’s normal area of 57.8 lakh hectares. This figure is also lower than the 47.2 lakh hectares recorded during the 1972 drought, making it worse in absolute terms despite being a smaller share of normal conditions. The Maharashtra government had declared drought across 74% of subdistricts on September 26, and the reported sowing area was down from 16.5 lakh hectares by November 17 in the prior season.

Division-wise, Latur led with 2.3 lakh hectares (16% of its normal average), followed by Pune at 1.8 lakh hectares, Amravati at 1.4 lakh hectares, Kolhapur at 1.2 lakh hectares, and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and Nagpur each near 1 lakh hectares. Nashik reported over 91,000 hectares while Konkan recorded the lowest sowing at just above 1,500 hectares.

Crop-wise data indicate farmers favored cereals (5.2 lakh hectares) and pulses (4.6 lakh hectares), bringing total foodgrains to nearly 10 lakh hectares, while oilseed sowing was limited to about 17% of its normal area at roughly 11,000 hectares.

The shortfall is attributed to monsoon deficits: the state received 804.4 mm during June-September against a normal 994.5 mm—a deficit of around 19%—with 19 of 36 districts recording deficient rainfall and Marathwada worst-hit, per The Times of India. The India Meteorological Department has linked the conditions to strong El Niño activity in the equatorial Pacific.

The report is based on figures as of November 16; no forecast or future projection was provided.
items.title: Maharashtra Records 17% of Normal Rabi Sowing Area, Below Even the 1972 Drought Level

items.summary:
Hours after Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Rs 4,280-crore Nitish Setu bridge in Vaishali, Bihar—connecting Kacchi Dargah in Patna district with Bidupur and comprising a 9.7 km main span plus roughly 10 km of approach roads—RJD workers staged a protest on Saturday (November 21). Supporters arrived by motorcycle to wave party flags, raise slogans backing Lalu Prasad Yadav and Tejashwi Yadav, remove posters, and pull down banners displaying the bridge's name. The demonstration reportedly lasted nearly 40 minutes before police intervened, according to India Today.

BJP spokesperson Neeraj Kumar Sharma condemned the RJD for disrupting a public event in pursuit of political gain, arguing that Bihar residents wanted infrastructure rather than disputes over posters. In response, RJD MP Sudhakar Singh defended the protest on Sunday (November 22), questioning why another inauguration ceremony was needed since the bridge had already been opened and alleging the NDA banners were placed fraudulently. Singh credited Tejashwi Yadav with advancing the project while also raising questions about Chief Minister Nitish Kumar's absence from the event, attributing it to an incident in which his son was reportedly pushed.

The protest stemmed partly from a private member's resolution moved by Tejashwi Yadav proposing that the bridge be named after Guru Gobind Singh rather than Nitish Kumar. He also asked the Centre to disclose its financial contribution toward the project and drew criticism from Punjab Cabinet Minister Harpal Singh Cheema over the decision to drop an earlier naming proposal.
items.title: RJD Workers Tear Down Banners at Nitish Setu After PM Modi Inaugurates Bihar Bridge

items.summary: The indefinite, round-the-clock sit-in protest by Karnataka's ASHA workers demanding a monthly honorarium of Rs 15,000 entered its sixth day on Sunday. The protesters accused the state government of reneging on an assurance and rejected Chief Minister D K Shivakumar's request for more time to consider their demand, stating they had waited one-and-a-half years and exhausted all avenues of discussion. Workers asserted that the agitation was a unanimous decision by representatives from all 31 districts rather than pressure from any organization or political party. They recalled former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah assuring them on January 10, 2025, that their honorarium would rise to Rs 10,000 following a four-day protest, an assurance he had publicized as Deputy Chief Minister and Congress president with the slogan 'Congress government stands by ASHA workers.' The workers cited repeated reminders of this promise during a Belagavi Assembly session on December 10, 2025, meetings with then Health Minister Dinesh Gundu Rao and present Health Minister U T Khader on August 18, 2026, and a strike notice submitted to the Chief Minister's Office, Chief Secretary and concerned department on November 2. They rejected the government's argument that conceding their demand could trigger similar protests from Anganwadi workers, mid-day meal workers and guest teachers, insisting there should be no discrimination among worker categories. The association also criticized the BJP-led Central government for failing to honor its promise of a Rs 1,500 increase in their honorarium. State Vice-President Rama T C stated that the protest would continue until the demand is fulfilled.
items.title: Karnataka ASHA Workers' Indefinite Honorarium Protest Enters Sixth Day

items.summary: In Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, the Crime Branch raided an illegal brothel operating at Hotel Nisarga in the Karodi area along the Dhule-Solapur Highway on Friday. Acting on confidential information received by Crime Branch officer Jagannath Menkudale and following instructions from senior officials, the team found that suspects were allegedly luring local women and women from other states into forced prostitution for financial gain. The operation rescued five women, who were shifted to a shelter home, while three suspects—Aditya Sunilkumar Pandey of Uttar Pradesh, Ravi Kashinath Pol of Kalyan in Thane district, and Sanjay Bansi Jadhav of Hirapur in Georai taluka of Beed district—were arrested. The lodge owner Kamlesh Bhalerao of Tisgaon and another suspect Devidas Munsi Rathod of Hatyaltanda in Basavakalyan taluka of Karnataka remain absconding, with police searching for them. Police seized cash, mobile phones and other items worth ₹56,200 during the raid. A case was registered at Daulatabad Police Station under Sections 3, 4 and 5 of the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act and Sections 143 and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The operation took place under guidance from Police Commissioner Pravin Pawar, Deputy Commissioner of Police (Crime) Shashikant Satav, Assistant Commissioner of Police (Crime) Poonam Patil, with Senior Police Inspector Gajanan Kalyankar and Sub-Inspector Jagannath Menkudale leading the team. The article also reports a separate incident in which unidentified thieves broke open an ATM at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Chowk in Wadwani early Saturday and fled with around ₹11.33 lakh, prompting CCTV review by police; however, no arrests or recovery figures were stated for this theft.
items.title: Crime Branch Raids Illegal Brothel at Hotel Nisarga in Karodi; Five Women Rescued and Three Suspects Arrested

items.summary: Hours after Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the six-lane, 9.76-km Nitish Setu on Saturday (November 21) at an estimated cost of Rs 4,280 crore, Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) workers triggered a disruption that lasted nearly 40 minutes by tearing down ruling NDA posters and banners while raising slogans in support of Lalu Prasad Yadav and Tejashwi Yadav. Videos of the incident went viral on social media, showing supporters waving party flags with police walking alongside them helplessly as most supporters rode motorcycles; the bridge connects Kacchi Dargah and Bidupur and is expected to improve connectivity between north and south Bihar while easing traffic congestion on the Mahatma Gandhi Setu. BJP spokesperson Neeraj Kumar Sharma accused RJD of political theatrics, stating that 'the people of Bihar want bridges and progress, not politics centred around tearing down posters.' The row centered partly on naming disputes: Tejashwi Yadav questioned why the bridge was named after Nitish Kumar rather than Guru Gobind Singh, whom he said had been proposed in a private member's resolution, alleging the decision was politically motivated to undermine Nitish Kumar's legacy and claiming Modi inaugurated a bridge already opened by Nitish Kumar about 1.5 years earlier ahead of elections; Tejashwi also challenged BJP over its contribution to construction. Punjab Cabinet Minister Harpal Singh Cheema separately condemned the Bihar government for abandoning an earlier proposal to name the bridge after Guru Gobind Singh, calling it 'deeply hurtful and completely unacceptable.' The text notes that these claims about funding contributions and prior inaugurations are allegations made by opposition leaders rather than confirmed facts.
items.title: RJD Workers Disrupt Nitish Setu Inauguration in Bihar's Vaishali Hours After PM Modi Opens Bridge

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced, via a November 22, 2026 post on X shared by the Prime Minister's Office (PMO), an ex-gratia of Rs 2 lakh from the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund (PMNRF) for the next of kin of each person killed in two separate accidents. In Gujarat's Kutch district, at least seven people were killed in a mishap; injured persons there would receive Rs 50,000 each. Separately, nine people died and several others were injured after a vehicle carrying pilgrims rammed into a parked truck near Shambhupura on the Kota-Udaipur highway in Rajasthan's Kota district. District Collector Rajesh Joshi stated that the accident occurred in the middle of the night involving 16 occupants from one family who were returning to Maharashtra after visiting Khatu Shyam Ji, and that post-mortems for the deceased were underway while injured persons received medical treatment; those injured would also receive Rs 50,000 each. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, President Droupadi Murmu, and former Rajasthan Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot expressed condolences over the Kota accident. The article provides no figures on total compensation amounts or number of beneficiaries beyond per-person ex-gratia values.
items.title: PM Modi announces Rs 2 lakh ex-gratia from PMNRF for Kutch and Kota accident victims
